heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Hire professionals in the DR without a local entity
heroData.description: Comprehensive EOR services to hire compliant talent in Dominican Republic in days, handling payroll, taxes, and benefits.
heroData.bestFor: Companies expanding to the DR without a local entity

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting a compliant employment contract in Spanish (mandatory). Contracts must specify wages, work hours (44 hours/week), and role duties. English translations are for reference only.

steps.title: DGT Registration
steps.description: Registering the employment contract with the Department of Labor (DGT-3 form) within the first week of employment.

steps.title: Social Security Enrollment
steps.description: Enrolling the employee with the Tesorería de la Seguridad Social (TSS) to cover Health (SFS), Pension (AFP), and Labor Risk (SRL) insurance.

steps.title: Tax Registration
steps.description: Setting up the employee in the DGII system (Dirección General de Impuestos Internos) for monthly income tax (ISR) withholdings.

steps.title: Bank Setup
steps.description: Collecting local bank account details for payroll. Payment in DOP (Dominican Pesos) is standard, though USD contracts are legal but paid in local currency equivalent.

rows.label: EOR Management Fee
values: Standard fee per employee. Percentage models (10-20%) also exist.

rows.label: Employer Social Security
values: Includes Pension (7.10%), Health (7.09%), Labor Risk (1.2%+), and INFOTEP (1%).

rows.label: Christmas Salary Accrual
values: Mandatory 13th month salary paid by Dec 20th. (1/12 of annual earnings).

rows.label: Severance Accrual
values: Accrual for 'Cesantía' (approx 21 days/year) is highly advised due to strict termination laws.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: The statutory probation period is 3 months. Termination during this period provides no severance pay, making it a critical evaluation window.

items.title: Minimum Wage 2025
items.text: As of April 2025, large company minimum wage is RD$27,988.80/month. Medium companies are RD$25,656.96/month.

items.title: 13th Month Salary
items.text: The 'Salario de Navidad' is mandatory, tax-exempt, and must be paid by December 20th. It equals one-twelfth of the year's total earnings.

items.title: Work Week
items.text: Standard work week is 44 hours. Typically 8 hours/day M-F and 4 hours on Saturday. Overtime is paid at 135% (regular) or 200% (holidays).

items.title: Cesantía (Severance)
items.text: Termination without cause requires severance: 21 days' salary per year of service (after 1 year). Short tenure (3-6mo) gets 6 days; (6mo-1yr) gets 13 days.

items.title: Notice Period (Preaviso)
items.text: Employers must give notice or pay in lieu: 7 days (3-6mo tenure), 14 days (6-12mo), or 28 days (1yr+).

items.title: Notification
items.text: Termination must be communicated to the Department of Labor within 48 hours to avoid penalties.

faqs.question: Can we terminate employees at will?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Desahucio' allows termination without cause, but it triggers mandatory severance (Cesantía) and notice pay (Preaviso).

faqs.question: Is the 13th month salary taxable?
faqs.answer: No, the statutory Christmas Salary is exempt from income tax (ISR) up to five times the minimum wage.

faqs.question: Do we need a physical address?
faqs.answer: The EOR provides the legal entity and address. However, for remote workers, their home address is registered as the workplace.

faqs.question: Can I transition from EOR to my own entity?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is a standard process. You will need to terminate the EOR contract (often recognizing seniority) and hire them under your new SRL.

faqs.question: Are background checks standard?
faqs.answer: Yes, requesting a 'Certificate of Good Conduct' is a common and legal practice during the hiring process.

steps.title: Incident Reporting
steps.description: Collating overtime, leaves, and absences. Note that overtime must be reported to the DGT.

steps.title: TSS Calculation
steps.description: Calculating Social Security contributions via the TSS (Tesorería de la Seguridad Social) portal. Invoices are generated automatically.

steps.title: Tax Calculation (ISR)
steps.description: Applying the progressive Income Tax (ISR) rates to the net taxable income (after SS deductions).

steps.title: Payment Processing
steps.description: Disbursing net salaries to employees. Electronic transfers (ACH) via local banks (Banco Popular, BHD) are standard.

steps.title: Filings
steps.description: Paying the TSS invoice by the 3rd working day of the following month and filing IR-3 tax forms with DGII by the 10th.

rows.label: Pension (AFP)
values: Capped at 20 minimum wages (RD$433,496 as of April 2025).

rows.label: Family Health (SFS)
values: Capped at 10 minimum wages (RD$216,748 as of April 2025).

rows.label: Labor Risk (SRL)
values: Based on company risk level. Capped at 4 minimum wages.

rows.label: INFOTEP
values: Technical training tax on total payroll.

rows.label: Income Tax (ISR)
values: Progressive rates apply above exemption threshold (~RD$34k/mo).

items.title: Christmas Salary
items.text: Mandatory 13th month pay. It is the sum of all earnings in the year divided by 12. Must be paid by Dec 20.

items.title: Vacation Leave
items.text: 14 working days paid vacation after 1 year of service. After 5 years, it increases to 18 working days.

items.title: Profit Sharing
items.text: Companies must distribute 10% of annual net profits to employees (Bonificación), capped at 45 days' salary (for <3 years tenure) or 60 days (3+ years).

items.title: Payment Deadlines
items.text: TSS payments are strictly due within the first 3 working days of the month. Late fees are high (approx 5% per month).

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.text: 14 weeks of paid maternity leave. The employer pays 50%, and Social Security subsidizes 50% (up to caps).

items.title: Electronic Payslips
items.text: Digital payslips are legal but must be accessible to the employee.

steps.title: Day 1-5: Updates
steps.description: Gather all incidents (new hires, leaves, overtime) for the pay period.

steps.title: Day 6-10: Calculation
steps.description: Process regular pay and TSS deductions. TSS invoices are usually generated electronically.

steps.title: Day 15 & 30: Payday
steps.description: Disburse salaries. Bi-monthly (quincenal) payment is the cultural norm in DR.

steps.title: Next Month Day 3: TSS Payment
steps.description: Deadline to pay the Social Security Treasury invoice to cover health and pension.

steps.title: Next Month Day 10: IR-3 Filing
steps.description: Deadline to file and remit the Income Tax (ISR) withholdings to the DGII.

faqs.question: What is the tax-free income threshold?
faqs.answer: Annual income up to RD$416,220.00 (approx RD$34,685/month) is exempt from Income Tax (ISR).

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, performance bonuses and profit sharing are subject to income tax. The 13th month Christmas salary is exempt.

faqs.question: How is overtime calculated?
faqs.answer: Hours over 44/week are paid at +35%. Hours on holidays or non-working days are paid at +100%.

faqs.question: Is severance payment taxed?
faqs.answer: Severance (Auxilio de Cesantía and Preaviso) is generally exempt from Income Tax, but any accrued vacation or bonus paid out is taxable.

faqs.question: Can I pay in USD?
faqs.answer: Contracts can be denominated in USD, but payments are typically made in DOP at the official exchange rate of the payment day.

rows.label: Income Tax (ISR)
values: Progressive rates apply after ~34,685 DOP monthly exemption.

rows.label: INFOTEP
values: Vocational training tax on gross payroll.

items.title: Christmas Salary
items.text: Mandatory. Equal to 1/12th of total annual earnings. Must be paid by December 20th. It is tax-exempt.

faqs.question: Is the 13th month taxed?
faqs.answer: No, the 'Salario de Navidad' is exempt from ISR and social security deductions up to a certain high cap.

faqs.question: What is the minimum wage?
faqs.answer: It varies by company size, ranging roughly from DOP 14k to 25k (2025 rates).

faqs.question: Is there a cap on SFS?
faqs.answer: Yes, SFS contributions are capped at 10 minimum wages. AFP is capped at 20 minimum wages.

faqs.question: Are lunch stipends taxed?
faqs.answer: Generally taxable unless they are part of a collective facility (cafeteria) or strictly for work purposes.

heroData.title: Company Incorporation in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Form your SRL in the DR
heroData.description: Step-by-step guide to registering a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SRL), obtaining your RNC, and starting business operations.
heroData.bestFor: Entrepreneurs and businesses establishing a local presence

steps.title: Name Registration (ONAPI)
steps.description: Registering the Trade Name (Nombre Comercial) with ONAPI. This is the first mandatory step to ensure name exclusivity.

steps.title: Bylaws & Assembly
steps.description: Drafting the Corporate Bylaws and holding the Constituent Assembly. Documents must be in Spanish.

steps.title: Incorporation Tax (DGII)
steps.description: Paying the capitalization tax (1% of authorized capital) to the DGII.

steps.title: Mercantile Registry
steps.description: Filing documents with the Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) to obtain the Mercantile Registry Certificate.

steps.title: Tax ID (RNC)
steps.description: Obtaining the Registro Nacional del Contribuyente (RNC) from the DGII. This is your company's permanent tax ID.

rows.label: Minimum Capital
values: ~USD $2,500. Must be fully subscribed and paid.

rows.label: Registration Fees
values: Chamber of Commerce and ONAPI filing fees.

rows.label: Legal Fees
values: Standard lawyer fees for drafting and processing.

items.title: Shareholders
items.text: Minimum of 2 shareholders, maximum of 50. Foreign individuals or entities are allowed to hold 100% ownership.

items.title: Management
items.text: Must have at least one Manager (Gerente). They can be a foreigner and do not strictly need to reside in the DR, though it is recommended for banking.

items.title: Timeline
items.text: The entire process typically takes 4 to 7 weeks depending on bureaucracy and document readiness.

list: Register with the Department of Labor (DGT).
Register with the TSS (Social Security Treasury).
Open a corporate bank account (requires RNC and physical presence often).
Obtain NCF (Comprobantes Fiscales) numbers from DGII.

steps.title: ONAPI Name Certificate
steps.description: Original certificate proving exclusive trade name reservation.

steps.title: Notarized Bylaws
steps.description: 'Estatutos Sociales' signed by all shareholders and authenticated by a notary public.

steps.title: Form RC-02
steps.description: Sworn declaration form for RNC issuance, including Annexes A (partners), B, and D (UBO).

steps.title: Bank Proof
steps.description: For EIRL, proof of deposit. For SRL, proof of share subscription.

steps.title: ID Copies
steps.description: Clear copies of Passports (foreigners) or Cédulas (locals) for all shareholders and managers.

faqs.question: Can I incorporate remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, by granting a Power of Attorney (POA) to a local lawyer. However, bank account opening often requires a personal visit.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need a registered fiscal address in the Dominican Republic for the DGII and Chamber of Commerce.

faqs.question: What is the corporate tax rate?
faqs.answer: The standard Corporate Income Tax (ISR) rate is 27% on net taxable income.

faqs.question: Can I be the sole shareholder?
faqs.answer: Not for an SRL, which requires at least 2 shareholders. For a single owner, you must form an EIRL (Individual Limited Liability Enterprise).

faqs.question: How long does it take to open a bank account?
faqs.answer: It can take 2-4 weeks after incorporation. Banks enforce strict compliance/KYC checks.

heroData.title: Staffing & Talent Acquisition in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Recruit top talent in the DR
heroData.description: Strategies for finding, screening, and hiring local professionals in the Dominican Republic, including agency fees and work permits.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Leveraging local job boards like Aldaba, LinkedIn, and university networks. Bilingual talent (Spanish/English) is highly sought after.

steps.title: Screening
steps.description: Conducting interviews and skills assessments. Background checks (Certificate of Good Conduct) are standard practice.

steps.title: Offer Stage
steps.description: Presenting an offer letter. Note: binding employment relationships can form even before a written contract is signed if work begins.

steps.title: contracts
steps.description: Signing a formal written contract registered with the DGT to define the terms clearly and protect the employer.

items.title: Nationalization Rule (80/20)
items.text: By law, at least 80% of a company's workforce must be Dominican nationals. Foreigners can only make up 20%, usually in management or technical roles.

items.title: Process Steps
items.text: 1. Business Visa (Labor Purposes) -> 2. Temporary Residency -> 3. Work Permit. The full cycle can take 6-12 months.

items.title: Validity
items.text: Work permits is annually renewable. It is tied to the specific employer and residency status.

items.title: Key Sectors
items.text: Tourism, Hospitality, Call Centers (BPO), and Manufacturing (Free Zones) are the largest employment sectors.

items.title: Education
items.text: There is a strong pool of talent in Santo Domingo and Santiago. English proficiency is growing but varies.

items.title: Buscojobs & Aldaba
items.text: Leading local job boards for general staffing and mid-level roles.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.text: Dominant for professional, executive, and bilingual talent in Santo Domingo and Santiago.

items.title: University Partnerships
items.text: Universities like INTEC and PUCMM have strong career centers for hiring fresh engineering and business graduates.

faqs.question: Can we hire foreigners freely?
faqs.answer: No, you must adhere to the 80% Dominican workforce quota. Exceptions exist for directors and technical specialists if no local is available.

faqs.question: What is the probation period?
faqs.answer: The statutory probation period is 3 months. During this time, termination is possible without severance.

faqs.question: Are fixed-term contracts allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, for specific projects or temporary needs. Determine 'Indefinite' vs 'Fixed-Term' carefully to avoid severance liabilities on non-renewal.

faqs.question: Are non-compete clauses enforceable?
faqs.answer: They are difficult to enforce. Courts often favor the employee's right to work, unless the restriction is compensated and very specific/limited.

faqs.question: What is the minimum vacation entitlement?
faqs.answer: Employees are entitled to 14 working days of paid vacation after 1 year of continuous service.

heroData.title: HRIS in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Digitize your HR operations
heroData.description: Platforms to manage employee data, payroll, and compliance with Dominican record-keeping laws (SIRLA & TSS).

steps.title: SIRLA Registration
steps.description: Employers must use the 'Sistema Integrado de Registro Laboral' (SIRLA) to register new hires (Form DGT-3) and annual personnel lists (DGT-4).

steps.title: TSS Portal
steps.description: The Social Security Treasury (TSS) portal is mandatory for managing monthly social security contributions and employee changes.

steps.title: Digital Payslips
steps.description: While physical signatures were traditional, digital receipt acknowledgments are increasingly accepted if the employee consents.

steps.title: Attendance Tracking
steps.description: The Labor Code mandates strict recording of work hours and overtime. Digital time tracking within an HRIS is highly recommended.

items.title: 10-Year Rule
items.text: Payroll records, contracts, and attendance logs must be retained for at least 10 years for DGII and Ministry of Labor audits.

items.title: Law 172-13 (Privacy)
items.text: Employees must consent to the processing of their personal data. They have the right to access and rectify their records (Habeas Data).

items.title: Consent Forms
items.text: Include a data processing consent clause in the employment contract to comply with Law 172-13.

rows.label: Global HRIS PEPM
values: Per Employee Per Month. Standard for platforms like BambooHR, Deel, etc.

rows.label: Local Payroll Module
values: Add-on for ensuring local tax/TSS calculation accuracy.

rows.label: Implementation
values: Setup fees depending on complexity and historical data migration.

items.title: Written Consent
items.text: Employers using fingerprint or facial recognition time clocks must obtain specific, written consent from each employee explaining the purpose and duration of storage.

items.title: Right to Delete
items.text: Employees have the right to demand the deletion of their biometric data upon termination of employment.

items.title: Compliance Audit
items.text: Ensure your HRIS vendor encrypts biometric templates and does not store raw images, complying with Law 172-13 security standards.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, Law 126-02 recognizes digital signatures and electronic documents as legally binding.

faqs.question: Can we store data abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must ensure security measures comply with Law 172-13 regarding international data transfers.

faqs.question: Is biometric time-tracking legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, but strictly regulated by Law 4-23. You cannot make it mandatory without obtaining explicit written consent first.

faqs.question: Do we need to register the specific software?
faqs.answer: Not the software itself, but reliance on digital reporting for payroll (TSS) and labor (SIRLA) requires authorized access credentials.

faqs.question: How long must we keep digital records?
faqs.answer: Labor and tax records must be retained for a minimum of 10 years to satisfy potential audits by DGII or the Ministry of Labor.

heroData.title: Accounting in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Manage DR taxes and E-Invoicing
heroData.description: Guide to corporate taxation (ISR), ITBIS (VAT), and the mandatory Electronic Invoicing (e-CF) system.

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax (ISR)
values: Of net taxable income. Standard flat rate.

rows.label: ITBIS (VAT)
values: Standard rate. Reduced 16% rate applies to certain food products.

rows.label: Asset Tax
values: Applied to total assets annually, creditable against ISR.

rows.label: Withholding (Dividends)
values: Withholding tax on dividends paid to shareholders.

steps.title: Monthly ITBIS (IT-1)
steps.description: Must be filed and paid by the 20th of the following month.

steps.title: Monthly Retentions (IR-17)
steps.description: Withholding taxes on other payments must be filed by the 10th of the following month.

steps.title: Annual ISR (IR-2)
steps.description: Corporate income tax return due 120 days after the fiscal year-end (e.g., April 30th).

steps.title: Asset Tax
steps.description: Filed jointly with the IR-2 return.

items.title: Mandatory Adoption
items.text: Law 32-23 mandates e-invoicing. Large taxpayers are already transitioning. Micro/Small businesses have until May 2026.

items.title: Requirements
items.text: You need a valid Digital Certificate from an INDOTEL-authorized issuer and DGII-certified software.

items.title: Free Billing
items.text: The DGII offers a free portal for small taxpayers issuing fewer than 150 invoices/month.

items.title: Exempt Goods
items.text: Basic foods (bread, milk, eggs, meats), medicines, educational materials, and fertilizers are exempt.

items.title: Service Exports
items.text: Services exported for consumption abroad are zero-rated (0% ITBIS).

list: Validate all received e-CFs (Electronic Invoices) in the DGII portal.
Reconcile TSS (Social Security) invoice against payroll ledger.
File and pay IT-1 (ITBIS/VAT) by the 20th.
File and pay IR-17 (Other Retentions) by the 10th.
Update Fixed Asset Ledger for any new acquisitions (Category 2 & 3 assets).

faqs.question: Can I choose my fiscal year?
faqs.answer: Yes, common options are Dec 31, Mar 31, Jun 30, or Sep 30.

faqs.question: Is foreign income taxable?
faqs.answer: Generally, the DR uses a territorial tax system, but financial income from abroad is taxable for residents.

faqs.question: When is an external audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: If gross income exceeds 100 minimum wages (approx. RD$2.8M) or if the company holds debt/issues securities.

faqs.question: Can I keep books in USD?
faqs.answer: No, accounting records must be maintained in Dominican Pesos (DOP). You can maintain parallel books in USD for reporting, but statutory books are in DOP.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late filing?
faqs.answer: Late filings incur a 10% surcharge on the first month and 4% for subsequent months, plus 1.1% cumulative interest.

steps.title: Identify Obligated Subjects
steps.description: Law 155-17 expands 'obligated subjects' to include lawyers, accountants, real estate agents, and construction firms, not just banks.

steps.title: KYC Procedures
steps.description: Implement rigorous Know Your Client (KYC) protocols to identify the ultimate beneficiaries of transactions.

steps.title: Report to UAF
steps.description: Suspicious activities must be reported to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) within 5 days.

items.title: Mandatory Registry
items.text: Companies must register any individual owning >20% of shares as a UBO with the DGII.

items.title: Annual Updates
items.text: UBO information must be updated annually in the tax filings or whenever a change in ownership occurs.

items.title: Privacy
items.text: The UBO registry is not public; it is accessible only by the tax authorities (DGII) and financial regulators.

items.title: Real Estate Limit
items.text: Cash payments for real estate are prohibited for amounts exceeding DOP 1,000,000.

items.title: Vehicle Limit
items.text: Cash payments for motor vehicles are limited to DOP 500,000.

items.title: Corporate Shares
items.text: Cash payments for buying/selling shares are limited to DOP 250,000.

steps.title: Identify Beneficiaries
steps.description: Identify all natural persons who ultimately own or control >20% of the company shares or voting rights.

steps.title: Complete Annex D
steps.description: Fill out Annex D of form RC-02 (or the specific UBO declaration form for existing entities) with ID details and % ownership.

steps.title: Submission
steps.description: Submit via the DGII Virtual Office. This is mandatory for obtaining an RNC and opening bank accounts.

steps.title: Annual Update
steps.description: Confirm or update UBO information annually when filing the IR-2 corporate tax return.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for non-compliance with AML?
faqs.answer: Fines can be substantial, and criminal liability (imprisonment) applies to individuals involved in money laundering schemes.

faqs.question: Who must file UBO info?
faqs.answer: All companies (SRL, SA, SAS) registered in the DR must identify and report their beneficial owners.

faqs.question: Is the UBO registry public?
faqs.answer: No, the information is confidential and accessible only by the DGII and competent authorities (UAF, Superintendencies).

faqs.question: Do I need a Compliance Officer?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Obligated Subjects' (banks, real estate, precious metals dealers, casinos) must appoint a Compliance Officer.

faqs.question: What is the CASH limit for real estate?
faqs.answer: Cash transactions for real estate are strictly capped at RD$1,000,000. Higher amounts must be banked.

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax (ISR)
values: Flat rate on net taxable income.

rows.label: Capital Gains Tax
values: Treated as ordinary income. No long-term holding discount.

rows.label: Personal Income Tax
values: Progressive scale. Top rate applies above ~867k DOP/year.

steps.title: Exempt Income
steps.description: Annual income up to DOP 416,220 is tax-free (0% rate).

steps.title: 15% Bracket
steps.description: Income between DOP 416,220 and DOP 624,329 is taxed at 15%.

steps.title: 20% Bracket
steps.description: Income between DOP 624,329 and DOP 867,123 is taxed at 20%.

steps.title: 25% Top Rate
steps.description: Income exceeding DOP 867,123 annually is taxed at 25%.

items.title: Double Taxation Treaties
items.text: The Dominican Republic has DTTs with Spain and Canada. A limited agreement exists with the USA (FATCA/Exchange of Info).

items.title: Foreign Financial Income
items.text: While generally legally territorial, Dominican tax residents are taxed on income from foreign financial investments.

items.title: Currently Exempt
items.text: As of mid-2025, foreign digital services (Netflix, Spotify, etc.) are NOT subject to ITBIS (VAT).

items.title: Decree Repealed
items.text: Decree 30-25, which attempted to levy 18% VAT on digital services, was repealed by Decree 107-25 in March 2025.

items.title: B2B Services
items.text: If a local company imports digital services (e.g., AWS, Google Ads), they must self-assess and pay the 18% ITBIS (Reverse Charge) and 27% Withholding if deemed Dominican-source income.

faqs.question: Are capital gains taxed differently?
faqs.answer: No, capital gains are added to ordinary income and taxed at the standard corporate rate of 27%.

faqs.question: What is the 1% asset tax?
faqs.answer: A minimum tax of 1% is applied to the company's total assets. It acts as an Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) if it exceeds the ISR liability.

faqs.question: Are digital services subject to VAT?
faqs.answer: B2C foreign digital services are currently exempt. B2B imports of services are subject to reverse-charge VAT and withholding.

faqs.question: What is the dividend tax rate?
faqs.answer: Dividends paid to residents or non-residents are subject to a final 10% withholding tax.

faqs.question: Is there a wealth tax?
faqs.answer: Individuals pay a 1% Real Estate Property Tax (IPI) on the total value of properties exceeding ~RD$9.8 million.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal Contracts in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Contract Law and Digital Signatures
heroData.description: Essentials of Dominican contract law, valid jurisdictions, and the legal status of digital signatures (Law 126-02).

steps.title: Civil Code Basis
steps.description: Contracts must meet four conditions: consent, capacity, rigorous object definition, and lawful cause (Article 1108).

steps.title: Language
steps.description: While English contracts are valid between private parties, a Spanish translation by a certified interpreter is required for court enforcement.

steps.title: Choice of Law
steps.description: Dominican courts respect foreign choice of law clauses, provided they do not violate local public policy (e.g., Law 173 on agency protection).

items.title: Legal Validity
items.text: Law 126-02 grants electronic documents and digital signatures the same legal weight as handwritten ones.

items.title: Certification
items.text: For higher legal presumption (Secure Digital Signature), use a certificate from an INDOTEL-authorized provider.

items.title: Arbitration
items.text: The CRC (Santo Domingo) and IACSDRD are common venues. The DR follows Law 489-08 for commercial arbitration.

items.title: Local Courts
items.text: Civil and Commercial courts handle contract disputes. Proceedings can be lengthy; arbitration is often preferred for speed.

list: Clear definition of 'Just Cause' for termination (Art. 88 Labor Code).
Intellectual Property assignment (Cesión de Derechos) for created works.
Specific work schedule (Horario) to define overtime liability.

faqs.question: Can we use US law for the contract?
faqs.answer: Yes, but local labor laws and 'public order' statutes (like agency protections) will override foreign law choices.

faqs.question: Is notarization required?
faqs.answer: Not strictly for all validity, but highly recommended for enforcement. Digital notarization is evolving under Law 126-02.

faqs.question: Is a trial period automatic?
faqs.answer: Yes, the first 3 months are considered a statutory probation period (no severance if terminated).

faqs.question: Can I enforce a non-compete?
faqs.answer: Only if limited in time and geography, and if the employee is compensated for the restriction. Courts often void broad bans.

heroData.title: Software Solutions in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: NCF and TSS Compliant Tools
heroData.description: Top local software for handling Electronic Invoicing (e-CF), payroll (TSS), and tax reporting.

rows.label: Edicom / Gosocket
values: Custom pricing. Great for high volume.

steps.title: Check NCF Capabilities

steps.title: TSS Integration
steps.description: Payroll modules should export files compatible with the SUIR system covering social security contributions.

steps.title: Certification
steps.description: Ensure the provider is on the DGII's list of certified e-CF developers.

items.title: E-Invoicing Authorization
items.text: Before using any software, you must formally request authorization to issue e-CFs via the DGII virtual office.

items.title: Local vs Global
items.text: Global ERPs (NetSuite, SAP) often require a local 'fiscalization' middleware to handle Dominican NCF/Tax reporting.

items.title: E-Invoicing Authorization
items.text: Before using any software, you must formally request authorization to issue e-CFs via the DGII virtual office.

items.title: Local vs Global
items.text: Global ERPs (NetSuite, SAP) often require a local 'fiscalization' middleware to handle Dominican NCF/Tax reporting.

items.title: Digital Certificate
items.text: You must obtain a digital certificate from an accredited CA (e.g., Avansi) to sign e-CFs legally.

faqs.question: Is Quickbooks NCF compliant?
faqs.answer: Not natively. You will likely need a third-party plugin or connector to handle Dominican fiscal receipts.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for e-invoicing?
faqs.answer: Large taxpayers are already mandated. Small businesses have until May 2026.

faqs.question: Is pirated software a risk?
faqs.answer: Yes, ONDA (Copyright Office) conducts raids. Using licensed software is critical for corporate compliance.

faqs.question: Are cloud solutions accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, cloud-based accounting and HRIS are fully legal as long as data privacy norms are met.

heroData.title: Marketing in Dominican Republic
heroData.subtitle: Agencies and Advertisement Laws
heroData.description: Directory of top digital agencies and summary of ProConsumidor advertising regulations.

steps.title: Alcohol Ads
steps.description: Banned on TV between 6 AM and 10 PM. Banned on Radio 4 PM - 6 PM.

steps.title: Tobacco Ads
steps.description: Strictly limited to 9 PM - 6 AM on all electronic media. Health warnings ('Fumar es perjudicial') are mandatory.

steps.title: Misleading Ads
steps.description: ProConsumidor actively monitors and sanctions misleading claims. Truth in advertising is legally enforced.

items.title: Social Media
items.text: Dominicans are heavy social media users (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok). Influencer marketing is highly effective.

items.title: Language
items.text: Campaigns must be in Spanish to be effective and legally compliant for official contracts/claims.

items.title: WhatsApp Business
items.text: Dominicans heavily use WhatsApp for commerce. It is a critical channel for B2C engagement and customer support.

items.title: Influencer Impact
items.text: Local micro-influencers often drive higher conversion than global ads. Note the 10% tax withholding on their fees.

items.title: Contest Rules
items.text: Raffles and contests (Giveaways) must be registered with ProConsumidor to be legal.

faqs.question: Are there restrictions on influencers?
faqs.answer: General truth-in-advertising laws apply. They must disclose sponsored content to avoid misleading consumers.

faqs.question: Can we execute English campaigns?
faqs.answer: You can, but it limits your audience to expats and tourists. Locals expect Spanish.

faqs.question: What is the influencer tax?
faqs.answer: Companies must withhold 10% ISR from payments to individuals (influencers) for services rendered.

faqs.question: Is email marketing regulated?
faqs.answer: Yes, spam laws require an opt-out mechanism, though enforcement is looser than generally seen in EU.
